in_hebrew.name: סימונה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: סימונה היא שם עברי שמקורו בשם 'שמעון', שפירושו 'הוא שומע' או 'שמע ה''. השם סימונה ניתן לנשים ומשמעו 'היא שומעת' או 'משמעת'. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב הנוצרים ומשויך לאחד מ-12 בניו של יעקב, שמעון, שזכה לשמע בקול ה'.

in_greek.name: Σιμόνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σιμόνη προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα 'Σίμων', που σημαίνει 'ακροατής' ή 'ακούω'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Σίμων αναφέρεται σε πολλούς ανθρώπους, συμπεριλαμβανομένου του Σίμων Πέτρος, ενός από τους 12 αποστόλους του Ιησού Χριστού. Το όνομα Σιμόνη έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί στην Εκκλησία από τους πρώτους χρόνους και συμβολίζει την ακοή και την υπακοή στον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Simona
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Simona is derived from the Hebrew name 'Shimon', which means 'he who hears'. The name was adopted into Latin as 'Simona', and it signifies a person who is obedient and attentive to the voice of God. In the early Christian Church, the name Simona was used to denote a woman who was devoted to her faith and willing to listen to and follow God's will.

in_english.name: Simona
in_english.long_meaning: The name Simona originates from the Hebrew name 'Shimon', which means 'he who hears'. The feminine form, Simona, signifies 'she who hears' or 'listener'. In Christian tradition, the name Simona represents a person who is attentive to God's voice and willing to obey His will. The name has been used in various Christian cultures, symbolizing spiritual receptivity and devotion. Historically, the name Simona has been associated with Saint Simon, one of Jesus' twelve apostles, and has been used in various forms across Europe.

data.cultural_impact: The name Simona has a rich cultural history, with roots in the ancient Hebrew tradition. Simona shares its origins with the male name Simon, which was a common name in the New Testament. The name Simona adds a feminine touch to this venerable name, carrying with it a sense of ancient wisdom and spiritual depth. Over the centuries, the name has been popular in various parts of Europe, particularly in Italy and Spain, and continues to be appreciated for its unique cultural connections to the past.

historical_references.reference: Simona Stylites, a Syrian woman who lived as a hermit on a pillar during the early 5th century AD, is believed to have inspired the name 'Simona'. She lived for over 50 years on a 12-meter high pillar near Antioch in Syria, attracting many pilgrims and followers.

Simona of Bethany is mentioned in the New Testament of the Bible. She is known for anointing Jesus' feet with expensive perfume and wiping them with her hair. This biblical reference possibly influenced the naming of girls as 'Simona' in Christian communities.
